title: Perfect factorization of maps to supported quasi-coherent complexes
statement: Let Y be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let V be a quasi-compact open, and work in its derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. Let P be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], and let K have quasi-coherent cohomology and zero derived restriction to V. Every map f:P → K factors as P → R → K, where R is perfect and its derived restriction to V is zero.

source.place: Proof, finite perfect factorization paragraph, generalized from the structure sheaf to any perfect source; Tags 0E4G, 094A and 09SP

proof.text: Perfect P has quasi-coherent cohomology. Let A=D_QCoh(Y), install its triangulated and isomorphism-closed structures and its universe-u coproducts, which agree with ambient coproducts. Restriction vanishing of K implies vanishing of each homology stalk on V, using the existing private stalk_subsingleton_of_restriction_zero from SupportedKoszulRelativeDetector, accessed with import all. Choose a supported perfect generator G and the supplied telescope of K starting with zero.

P is compact in A. Reindex the ambient countable cofan by ULift natural numbers in universe u. Its point is in A by coproduct closure; restrict the ambient colimit universal property to A. Lift the telescope triangle to A with its inclusion shift comparison. The canonical identity-minus-transition map is conjugate to the supplied identity-minus-s. Apply compact_hom_hocolim with compact source P and target K; surjectivity and Types.jointly_surjective give one stage map whose composite into K is f.

The initial zero stage is the empty coproduct of shifts of G. Lift each ambient attaching cofan with the existing private ambient_shift_coproduct_iso from CompactGeneratorAmbientThick (accessed with import all), and lift its triangle to A using closure under triangles and inclusion shift comparisons. Inverse rotation makes the attaching object a coproduct of shifts G[m-1]. Apply compact_factorThrough_thickClosure with singleton compact family G to the finite-stage map. It factors through Q in the thick envelope of a finite coproduct of G. This handles stage zero without a separate case split.

Use the existing private perfect_thick_property from DerivedQCohCompactRepresentatives, accessed with import all, to give the perfect objects their triangulated retract-closed property. Its proof uses perfect_of_iso and perfect_thick_closure, including the split retract triangle and the zero object as a retract of G; none of these helper proofs is copied here. The property of restricting to zero on V is also triangulated and retract-closed: restriction commutes with shifts and distinguished triangles, and maps retract equations. G has this property by supported_derived_restriction_zero. Intersect the properties and pull back to A. Finite products and the finite biproduct/coproduct isomorphisms put the finite sum of G in this property. The universal property of triangEnvelope puts Q there. Compose Q to the finite stage with its map into K, and use the two factorization equations.

proof_origin.place: Finite factorization argument; generalized telescope transport, with existing private coproduct, perfect thick-property and stalk helpers reused through import all rather than reproved

mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about derived fractions and bounded representatives, no support-preserving perfect factorization.

Mathlib: no hits. Local library: CompactGeneratorAmbientThick only handles the identity of a compact telescope target; its private transport proof was generalized here to an arbitrary compact-source map.

lean.statement: theorem supported_perfect_factorization (Y : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (V : Y.Opens) [CompactSpace (V : Set Y)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : Y.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))] (P K : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (hP : Scheme.IsPerfect Y P) (hK : schemeDerivedQCohProperty Y K) (hzero : IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) V).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) (f : P ⟶ K) : ∃ (R : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (a : P ⟶ R) (b : R ⟶ K), Scheme.IsPerfect Y R ∧ IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) V).mapDerivedCategory.obj R) ∧ a ≫ b = f
